thread:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: GPU pool exhausted in prod cluster us-west-2. autoscaler reported repeated failures adding nodes. severity=P1 :rotating_light:

oncall-alex: on it — pulling up metrics and queue stats. can someone confirm affected customer lists?

sre-jen: seeing queue depth spike on inference-requests queue. token throttles increasing. 503s on /v1/generate for some tenants.

infra-miguel: autoscaler logs show AWS nodegroup create failing with launch template validation error. snippet: 
```
E0424 14:20:11.123456 autoscaler.go:312] Failed to create nodegroup (gpu-pool-2): InvalidLaunchTemplate: Launch template version 0 doesn't exist
```

eng-ryan: hmm we rolled a launch template patch yesterday (gpu-image + taint change). maybe the new version didn't publish to the nodegroup config.

oncall-alex: customer impact: Prod responses delayed >2s median, some requests timed out. I'll notify support to flag top 10 tenants. Lina, can you prepare status blurb?

prodops-lina: on it. Drafting: "We are investigating increased latency and intermittent timeouts for inference in us-west-2; engineering is working on capacity and autoscaler issues."

support-kate: already triaging tickets; customers A and B are seeing failures. Marking incident for SLA escalation.

sre-jen: current cluster GPU utilization across pools: 98%. backlog L7 queue length +420% in last 6m. autoscaler attempted 6 creates in last 10m, all failed.

infra-miguel: going to try manual nodegroup scaling to unblock. creating temporary nodegroup with working launch template version.

eng-ryan: quick mitigation: can we also temporarily remove the taint requirement on scheduled GPU node label so pods can land on non-tainted nodes? risky but might help.

sre-jen: prefer manual nodegroup to avoid changing scheduling rules. but removing taint might schedule non-GPU workloads onto GPUs. need to be careful.

infra-miguel: manual nodegroup create started. aws cli: 
```
aws eks create-nodegroup --cluster-name prod-cluster --nodegroup-name gpu-temp-1799 --scaling-config minSize=0,maxSize=10,desiredSize=4 --launch-template name=gpu-prod-lt,version=15
```

deploy-bot: Nodegroup creation event: gpu-temp-1799 status=CREATE_IN_PROGRESS

oncall-alex: meanwhile, I'm routing new low-priority inference traffic to dedicated fallback region (us-east) and switching model routing to smaller model variant for free-tier tenants. This will reduce pressure.

prodops-lina: posted status: "We are mitigating a capacity issue in us-west-2, routing lower-priority traffic to another region and provisioning temporary nodes. We'll update in 30 minutes."

eng-ryan: also enabling prefix caching for long-running chat sessions to reduce token work (quick config change). Doing canary update on the caching toggles.

sre-jen: autoscaler still failing: new error in logs: 
```
E0424 14:29:02.987654 autoscaler.go:388] NodeGroup creation failed: UnauthorizedOperation: You are not authorized to perform this operation on launch template version 15
```

infra-miguel: that's IAM — role used by autoscaler doesn't have ec2:CreateLaunchTemplateVersion or ec2:RunInstances on the new LT versions. Looking at recent policy change from infra-iam PR #2045.

oncall-alex: can we temporarily grant those permissions to the autoscaler role? need an immediate fix.

infra-miguel: I can patch the role with least-privilege permitting RunInstances for that specific LT. Doing now.

infra-miguel: patched IAM, retrying autoscaler create.

depoy-bot: (system) nodegroup gpu-temp-1799 status=CREATE_COMPLETE

eng-ryan: good. pods are starting to schedule onto gpu-temp-1799. Backlog processing rate increasing.

sre-jen: queue length starting to drop, token throttles falling. watch for stability.

support-kate: customers A,B reporting partial restoration. marking impacted tickets as "service restored, under monitoring".

oncall-alex: follow-up: we need to identify root cause: why did nodegroup creation fail originally? was it missing LT version or IAM or both?

infra-miguel: hypothesis: deploy pipeline published a new launch template version (v17) and updated nodegroup config for gpu-pool-2, but not all nodegroups referenced the new version. simultaneously, an IAM tightening PR removed broad RunInstances/LaunchTemplate version creation privileges from the autoscaler role — intended, but we missed the exception for autoscaler. result: autoscaler attempted to create nodes referencing the new template version or create a new version and got Unauthorized.

sre-jen: timeline check: LT change merged at 12:07, IAM PR merged at 12:12, autoscaler errors started 12:21, queue spike 12:22. aligns.

eng-ryan: action items from mitigation: 
- revert pipeline that applies LT v17 to consumers until we reconcile (or ensure nodegroup references existing version)
- add exception to IAM policy for autoscaler role or adopt more granular template version permissions
- add health check in rollout pipeline to validate nodegroup reference + autoscaler role permissions before LT publish

prodops-lina: I'll draft post-incident customer comms and update status page with timeline once we confirm.

oncall-alex: telemetry note: enable alert for autoscaler UnauthorizedOperation errors and a new composite alert for queue growth + create failures.

sre-jen: creating postmortem tracker ticket and assigning owners. copies to infra-miguel for IAM, eng-ryan for pipeline, and devex for rollout checklist.

infra-miguel: long-term fix: move autoscaler to use pre-provisioned launch template versions and disallow pipeline from making destructive LT edits without coordinated deployment window. also add test that simulates node creation with autoscaler role creds.

eng-ryan: also let's add a temporary automated fallback that if autoscaler create fails N times within M minutes, we trigger creation of the pre-approved temp nodegroup via infra pipeline (with safe LT and IAM) to avoid manual intervention.

prodops-lina: support update posted. customers notified. tracking SLA credits where appropriate.

oncall-alex: thanks team. I'll keep monitoring for next 2 hours then hand back to normal ops. any blockers on follow-ups?

sre-jen: none. capturing logs and putting into the incident ticket. adding decision record for "do not tighten autoscaler IAM policies without autoscaler validation test".

incident-bot: Incident closed to P2 after mitigation at 1799994600. follow-ups assigned: INC-2026-1799 (owners: infra-miguel, eng-ryan, prodops-lina).

support-kate: leaving notes for customers, will reopen if any regression. :white_check_mark:
